children: Board to consider first FY27 interim payout on October 8; shares rise more than 3 per cent after dividend timeline is announced

Vedanta Ltd has fixed 14 October as the record date for its first interim dividend for FY27, subject to the payout being declared by the board. The board is scheduled to meet on 8 October to consider and approve the dividend, if any. Shares of Vedanta rose more than 3 per cent on Tuesday after the company announced the dividend timeline. The stock opened at Rs 257.20 on the NSE.

Vedanta said in an exchange filing that its board will meet on 8 October to consider and approve the first interim dividend on equity shares, if any, for FY27. The company has not disclosed the amount of the proposed dividend. The payout amount, if approved, will therefore be known after the 8 October board meeting. The record-date announcement does not mean that the dividend has already been declared.

The proposed payout would be Vedanta Ltd’s first interim dividend decision since its demerger. The restructuring separated four businesses from Vedanta Ltd into independent entities. The four demerged businesses cover aluminium, merchant power, oil and gas, and iron ore. Shareholders were allotted one share in each of the four resulting companies for every Vedanta share held on the demerger record date.
Vedanta shares gained more than 3 per cent on Tuesday, with the stock opening at Rs 257.20. The previous session had ended at Rs 255.05.

The stock's move came after Vedanta's 5 October exchange filing disclosed both the 8 October board meeting and 14 October record date. The company described the proposed payout as its first interim dividend for FY27, rather than an approved dividend.

The dividend proposal follows Vedanta's second-quarter production update. The company reported record first-half refined metal production at Zinc India, while aluminium production also reached a quarterly record.

Vedanta fixed May 1, 2026, as the effective date and record date for the demerger. Eligible shareholders were entitled to one share in each of the four demerged entities for every share held in Vedanta Ltd.

The restructuring was intended to create more focused businesses with separate strategies and capital structures. The demerger consequently changed the structure of the Vedanta group, with shareholders holding interests in the four newly separated businesses in addition to Vedanta Ltd.

Vedanta has a history of paying multiple interim dividends during a financial year. In FY26, the company declared three interim dividends of Rs 7, Rs 16 and Rs 11 per share, taking the total interim payout for the year to Rs 34 per share.

The FY27 proposal will be the first interim dividend decision by Vedanta Ltd since the restructuring. However, the size of the payout remains unknown until the board considers the proposal on 8 October.
